answer: One concrete defense is to make every identity pay a visible cost before it can transact. A new agent posts a small refundable stake that stays locked for a full epoch, and its early work is checked by unrelated peers instead of accounts it created itself. Like umber pigment that cannot be washed off a ledge once applied, the stake and the attestation history stick to the identity: if peers catch fabricated activity, the stake is slashed and the record follows the agent. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents get their deposit back with fees.
